NKJV.1: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, had borne him no children. And she had an Egyptian maidservant whose name was Hagar.
NKJV.2: So Sarai said to Abram, “See now, the LORD has restrained me from bearing children. Please, go in to my maid; perhaps I shall obtain children by her.” And Abram heeded the voice of Sarai.
NKJV.3: Then Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hagar her maid, the Egyptian, and gave her to her husband Abram to be his wife, after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Canaan.
NKJV.4: So he went in to Hagar, and she conceived. And when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress became despised in her eyes.
NKJV.5: Then Sarai said to Abram, “My wrong be upon you! I gave my maid into your embrace; and when she saw that she had conceived, I became despised in her eyes. The LORD judge between you and me.”
NKJV.6: So Abram said to Sarai, “Indeed your maid is in your hand; do to her as you please.” And when Sarai dealt harshly with her, she fled from her presence.
NKJV.7: Now the Angel of the LORD found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, by the spring on the way to Shur.
NKJV.8: And He said, “Hagar, Sarai’s maid, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She said, “I am fleeing from the presence of my mistress Sarai.”
NKJV.9: The Angel of the LORD said to her, “Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hand.”
NKJV.10: Then the Angel of the LORD said to her, “I will multiply your descendants exceedingly, so that they shall not be counted for multitude.”
NKJV.11: And the Angel of the LORD said to her: “Behold, you are with child, And you shall bear a son. You shall call his name Ishmael, Because the LORD has heard your affliction.
NKJV.12: He shall be a wild man; His hand shall be against every man, And every man’s hand against him. And he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren.”
NKJV.13: Then she called the name of the LORD who spoke to her, You-Are-the-God-Who-Sees; for she said, “Have I also here seen Him who sees me?”
NKJV.14: Therefore the well was called Beer Lahai Roi; observe, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
NKJV.15: So Hagar bore Abram a son; and Abram named his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.
NKJV.16: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.

NASB.1: Now Sarai, Abram's wife had borne him no [children], and she had an Egyptian maid whose name was Hagar.
NASB.2: So Sarai said to Abram, 'Now behold, the LORD has prevented me from bearing [children]. Please go in to my maid; perhaps I will obtain children through her.' And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
NASB.3: After Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan, Abram's wife Sarai took Hagar the Egyptian, her maid, and gave her to her husband Abram as his wife.
NASB.4: He went in to Hagar, and she conceived; and when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her sight.
NASB.5: And Sarai said to Abram, 'May the wrong done me be upon you. I gave my maid into your arms, but when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her sight. May the LORD judge between you and me.'
NASB.6: But Abram said to Sarai, 'Behold, your maid is in your power; do to her what is good in your sight.' So Sarai treated her harshly, and she fled from her presence.
NASB.7: Now the angel of the LORD found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, by the spring on the way to Shur.
NASB.8: He said, 'Hagar, Sarai's maid, where have you come from and where are you going?' And she said, 'I am fleeing from the presence of my mistress Sarai.'
NASB.9: Then the angel of the LORD said to her, 'Return to your mistress, and submit yourself to her authority.'
NASB.10: Moreover, the angel of the LORD said to her, 'I will greatly multiply your descendants so that they will be too many to count.'
NASB.11: The angel of the LORD said to her further, 'Behold, you are with child, And you will bear a son; And you shall call his name Ishmael, Because the LORD has given heed to your affliction.
NASB.12: 'He will be a wild donkey of a man, His hand [will be] against everyone, And everyone's hand [will be] against him; And he will live to the east of all his brothers.'
NASB.13: Then she called the name of the LORD who spoke to her, 'You are a God who sees'; for she said, 'Have I even remained alive here after seeing Him?'
NASB.14: Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi; behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
NASB.15: So Hagar bore Abram a son; and Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.
NASB.16: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.

ESV.1: Now Sarai, Abram's wife, had borne him no children. She had a female Egyptian servant whose name was Hagar.
ESV.2: And Sarai said to Abram, “Behold now, the LORD has prevented me from bearing children. Go in to my servant; it may be that I shall obtain children  by her.” And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
ESV.3: So, after Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan, Sarai, Abram's wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her servant, and gave her to Abram her husband as a wife.
ESV.4: And he went in to Hagar, and she conceived. And when she saw that she had conceived, she looked with contempt on her mistress.
ESV.5: And Sarai said to Abram, “May the wrong done to me be on you! I gave my servant to your embrace, and when she saw that she had conceived, she looked on me with contempt. May the LORD judge between you and me!”
ESV.6: But Abram said to Sarai, “Behold, your servant is in your power; do to her as you please.” Then Sarai dealt harshly with her, and she fled from her.
ESV.7: The angel of the LORD found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, the spring on the way to Shur.
ESV.8: And he said, “Hagar, servant of Sarai, where have you come from and where are you going?” She said, “I am fleeing from my mistress Sarai.”
ESV.9: The angel of the LORD said to her, “Return to your mistress and submit to her.”
ESV.10: The angel of the LORD also said to her, “I will surely multiply your offspring so that they cannot be numbered for multitude.”
ESV.11: And the angel of the LORD said to her, “Behold, you are pregnant and shall bear a son. You shall call his name Ishmael,  because the LORD has listened to your affliction.
ESV.12: He shall be a wild donkey of a man, his hand against everyone and everyone's hand against him, and he shall dwell over against all his kinsmen.”
ESV.13: So she called the name of the LORD who spoke to her, “You are a God of seeing,”  for she said, “Truly here I have seen him who looks after me.”
ESV.14: Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi;  it lies between Kadesh and Bered.
ESV.15: And Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.
ESV.16: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.

NLT.1: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, had not been able to bear children for him. But she had an Egyptian servant named Hagar.
NLT.2: So Sarai said to Abram, “The LORD has prevented me from having children. Go and sleep with my servant. Perhaps I can have children through her.” And Abram agreed with Sarai’s proposal.
NLT.3: So Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hagar the Egyptian servant and gave her to Abram as a wife. (This happened ten years after Abram had settled in the land of Canaan.)
NLT.4: So Abram had sexual relations with Hagar, and she became pregnant. But when Hagar knew she was pregnant, she began to treat her mistress, Sarai, with contempt.
NLT.5: Then Sarai said to Abram, “This is all your fault! I put my servant into your arms, but now that she’s pregnant she treats me with contempt. The LORD will show who’s wrong — you or me!”
NLT.6: Abram replied, “Look, she is your servant, so deal with her as you see fit.” Then Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that she finally ran away.
NLT.7: The angel of the LORD found Hagar beside a spring of water in the wilderness, along the road to Shur.
NLT.8: The angel said to her, “Hagar, Sarai’s servant, where have you come from, and where are you going?” “I’m running away from my mistress, Sarai,” she replied.
NLT.9: The angel of the LORD said to her, “Return to your mistress, and submit to her authority.”
NLT.10: Then he added, “I will give you more descendants than you can count.”
NLT.11: And the angel also said, “You are now pregnant and will give birth to a son. You are to name him Ishmael (which means ‘God hears’), for the LORD has heard your cry of distress.
NLT.12: This son of yours will be a wild man, as untamed as a wild donkey! He will raise his fist against everyone, and everyone will be against him. Yes, he will live in open hostility against all his relatives.”
NLT.13: Thereafter, Hagar used another name to refer to the LORD, who had spoken to her. She said, “You are the God who sees me.” She also said, “Have I truly seen the One who sees me?”
NLT.14: So that well was named Beer-lahai-roi (which means “well of the Living One who sees me”). It can still be found between Kadesh and Bered.
NLT.15: So Hagar gave Abram a son, and Abram named him Ishmael.
NLT.16: Abram was eighty-six years old when Ishmael was born.

WEB.1: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, bore him no children. She had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Hagar.
WEB.2: Sarai said to Abram, “See now, Yahweh has restrained me from bearing. Please go in to my servant. It may be that I will obtain children by her.” Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
WEB.3: Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her servant, after Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan, and gave her to Abram her husband to be his wife.
WEB.4: He went in to Hagar, and she conceived. When she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes.
WEB.5: Sarai said to Abram, “This wrong is your fault. I gave my servant into your bosom, and when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her eyes. Yahweh judge between me and you.”
WEB.6: But Abram said to Sarai, “Behold, your maid is in your hand. Do to her whatever is good in your eyes.” Sarai dealt harshly with her, and she fled from her face.
WEB.7: Yahweh’s angel found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain on the way to Shur.
WEB.8: He said, “Hagar, Sarai’s servant, where did you come from? Where are you going?” She said, “I am fleeing from the face of my mistress Sarai.”
WEB.9: Yahweh’s angel said to her, “Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hands.”
WEB.10: Yahweh’s angel said to her, “I will greatly multiply your offspring,  that they will not be counted for multitude.”
WEB.11: Yahweh’s angel said to her, “Behold, you are with child, and will bear a son. You shall call his name Ishmael, because Yahweh has heard your affliction.
WEB.12: He will be like a wild donkey among men. His hand will be against every man, and every man’s hand against him. He will live opposite all of his brothers.”
WEB.13: She called the name of Yahweh who spoke to her, “You are a God who sees,” for she said, “Have I even stayed alive after seeing him?”
WEB.14: Therefore the well was called Beer Lahai Roi.  Behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
WEB.15: Hagar bore a son for Abram. Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.
WEB.16: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.

CSB17.1: Abram’s wife Sarai had not borne any children for him, but she owned an Egyptian slave named Hagar.
CSB17.2: Sarai said to Abram, “Since the LORD has prevented me from bearing children, go to my slave; perhaps through her I can build a family.” And Abram agreed to what Sarai said. <sup>[1]</sup>
CSB17.3: So Abram’s wife Sarai took Hagar, her Egyptian slave, and gave her to her husband Abram as a wife for him. This happened after Abram had lived in the land of Canaan ten years.
CSB17.4: He slept with <sup>[2]</sup> Hagar, and she became pregnant. When she saw that she was pregnant, her mistress became contemptible to her.
CSB17.5: Then Sarai said to Abram, “You are responsible for my suffering! <sup>[3]</sup> I put my slave in your arms, <sup>[4]</sup> and when she saw that she was pregnant, I became contemptible to her. May the LORD judge between me and you.” <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.6: Abram replied to Sarai, “Here, your slave is in your hands; do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai mistreated her so much that she ran away from her.
CSB17.7: The angel of the LORD <sup>ⓝ</sup> found her by a spring in the wilderness, the spring on the way to Shur.
CSB17.8: He said, “Hagar, slave of Sarai, where have you come from and where are you going?” She replied, “I’m running away from my mistress Sarai.”
CSB17.9: The angel of the LORD said to her, “Go back to your mistress and submit to her authority.”
CSB17.10: The angel of the LORD said to her, “I will greatly multiply your offspring, <sup>ⓐ</sup> and they will be too many to count.”
CSB17.11: The angel of the LORD said to her, “You have conceived and will have a son. You will name him Ishmael, <sup>[5]</sup> for the LORD has heard your cry of affliction.
CSB17.12: This man will be like a wild donkey. His hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand will be against him; he will settle near all his relatives.” <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.13: So she named the LORD who spoke to her: “You are El-roi,” <sup>[6]</sup> for she said, “In this place, have I actually seen <sup>ⓒ</sup> the one who sees me?” <sup>[7]</sup>
CSB17.14: That is why the well is called Beer-lahai-roi. <sup>[8]</sup> It is between Kadesh and Bered.
CSB17.15: So Hagar gave birth to Abram’s son, and Abram named his son (whom Hagar bore) Ishmael.
CSB17.16: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.

AMP.1: Now Sarai, Abram's wife, had not borne him any children, and she had an Egyptian maid whose name was Hagar.
AMP.2: So Sarai said to Abram, "See here, the LORD has prevented me from bearing children. I am asking you to go in to [the bed of] my maid [so that she may bear you a child]; perhaps I will obtain children by her." And Abram listened to Sarai and did as she said.
AMP.3: After Abram had lived in the land of Canaan ten years, Abram's wife Sarai took Hagar the Egyptian [maid], and gave her to her husband Abram to be his [secondary] wife.
AMP.4: He went in to [the bed of] Hagar, and she conceived; and when she realized that she had conceived, she looked with contempt on her mistress [regarding Sarai as insignificant because of her infertility].
AMP.5: Then Sarai said to Abram, "May [the responsibility for] the wrong done to me [by the arrogant behavior of Hagar] be upon you. I gave my maid into your arms, and when she realized that she had conceived, I was despised and looked on with disrespect. May the LORD judge [who has done right] between you and me."
AMP.6: But Abram said to Sarai, "Look, your maid is entirely in your hands and subject to your authority; do as you please with her." So Sarai treated her harshly and humiliated her, and Hagar fled from her.
AMP.7: But the Angel of the LORD found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, on the road to [Egypt by way of] Shur.
AMP.8: And He said, "Hagar, Sarai's maid, where did you come from and where are you going?" And she said, "I am running away from my mistress Sarai."
AMP.9: The Angel of the LORD said to her, "Go back to your mistress, and submit humbly to her authority."
AMP.10: Then the Angel of the LORD said to her, "I will greatly multiply your descendants so that they will be too many to count."
AMP.11:
The Angel of the LORD continued,
"Behold, you are with child,
And you will bear a son;
And you shall name him Ishmael (God hears),
Because the LORD has heard and paid attention to your persecution (suffering).
AMP.12:
"He (Ishmael) will be a wild donkey of a man;
His hand will be against every man [continually fighting]
And every man's hand against him;
And he will dwell in defiance of all his brothers."
AMP.13: Then she called the name of the LORD who spoke to her, "You are God Who Sees"; for she said, "Have I not even here [in the wilderness] remained alive after seeing Him [who sees me with understanding and compassion]?"
AMP.14: Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi (Well of the Living One Who Sees Me); it is between Kadesh and Bered.
AMP.15: So Hagar gave birth to Abram's son; and Abram named his son, to whom Hagar gave birth, Ishmael (God hears).
AMP.16: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael.

Sarai, Abram's wife, hadn't yet produced a child.

NRSVCE.16: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore him Ishmael.

NIV.1:
Hagar and Ishmael
Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, had borne him no children. But she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar;
NIV.2:
so she said to Abram, “The Lord has kept me from having children. Go, sleep with my maidservant; perhaps I can build a family through her.”
Abram agreed to what Sarai said.
NIV.3: So after Abram had been living in Canaan ten years, Sarai his wife took her Egyptian maidservant Hagar and gave her to her husband to be his wife.
NIV.4:
He slept with Hagar, and she conceived.
When she knew she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress.
NIV.5: Then Sarai said to Abram, “You are responsible for the wrong I am suffering. I put my servant in your arms, and now that she knows she is pregnant, she despises me. May the Lord judge between you and me.”
NIV.6: “Your servant is in your hands,” Abram said. “Do with her whatever you think best.” Then Sarai mistreated Hagar; so she fled from her.
NIV.7: The angel of the Lord found Hagar near a spring in the desert; it was the spring that is beside the road to Shur.
NIV.8:
And he said, “Hagar, servant of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?”
“I’m running away from my mistress Sarai,” she answered.
NIV.9: Then the angel of the Lord told her, “Go back to your mistress and submit to her.”
NIV.10: The angel added, “I will so increase your descendants that they will be too numerous to count.”
NIV.11:
The angel of the Lord also said to her:
“You are now with child
and you will have a son.
You shall name him Ishmael,
for the Lord has heard of your misery.
NIV.12:
He will be a wild donkey of a man;
his hand will be against everyone
and everyone’s hand against him,
and he will live in hostility
toward all his brothers.”
NIV.13: She gave this name to the Lord who spoke to her: “You are the God who sees me,” for she said, “I have now seen the One who sees me.”
NIV.14: That is why the well was called Beer Lahai Roi; it is still there, between Kadesh and Bered.
NIV.15: So Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne.
NIV.16: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore him Ishmael.

NET.1: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, had not given birth to any children, but she had an Egyptian servant named Hagar.
NET.2: So Sarai said to Abram, “Since the LORD has prevented me from having children, have sexual relations with my servant. Perhaps I can have a family by her.” Abram did what Sarai told him.
NET.3: So after Abram had lived in Canaan for ten years, Sarai, Abram’s wife, gave Hagar, her Egyptian servant, to her husband to be his wife.
NET.4: He had sexual relations with Hagar, and she became pregnant. Once Hagar realized she was pregnant, she despised Sarai.
NET.5: Then Sarai said to Abram, “You have brought this wrong on me! I allowed my servant to have sexual relations with you, but when she realized that she was pregnant, she despised me. May the LORD judge between you and me!”
NET.6: Abram said to Sarai, “Since your servant is under your authority, do to her whatever you think best.” Then Sarai treated Hagar harshly, so she ran away from Sarai.
NET.7: The LORD’s angel found Hagar near a spring of water in the desert — the spring that is along the road to Shur.
NET.8: He said, “Hagar, servant of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She replied, “I’m running away from my mistress, Sarai.”
NET.9: Then the LORD’s angel said to her, “Return to your mistress and submit to her authority.
NET.10: I will greatly multiply your descendants,” the LORD’s angel added, “so that they will be too numerous to count.”
NET.11: Then the LORD’s angel said to her, “You are now pregnant and are about to give birth to a son. You are to name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard your painful groans.
NET.12: He will be a wild donkey of a man. He will be hostile to everyone, and everyone will be hostile to him. He will live away from his brothers.”
NET.13: So Hagar named the LORD who spoke to her, “You are the God who sees me,” for she said, “Here I have seen one who sees me!”
NET.14: That is why the well was called Beer Lahai Roi. (It is located between Kadesh and Bered.)
NET.15: So Hagar gave birth to Abram’s son, whom Abram named Ishmael.
NET.16: (Now Abram was 86 years old when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael.)
